issue.body:
Jira Link: [[DB-326]](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-326)
This is a master issue tracking tasks to ensure user-visible transaction semantics in YSQL are the same as that of Postgres to the extent theoretically possible (i.e., barring any differences that stem from distributed nature of the database).

There are also some tasks/issues that don't exactly fall in the bucket of user-visible transaction semantics but are related to the transactional sub-system.

### Phase 1 - Miscellaneous items

- #1199
- #4291
- #1237
- #9467
- #9929
- #2742
- #11760
- #12166
- #11761
- #11571
- #12168
- #12325
- #12184
- #14985
- #14991

### Phase 2 - READ COMMITTED isolation level (present as a beta feature in 2.14 and 2.15)

- #13557 (detailed roadmap present in the github issue)
- #15272

### Phase 3 - Wait queue based pessimistic locking

This feature will support pessimistic locking behaviour for all isolation levels (READ COMMITTED will already have a basic implementation of this in Phase 2, this will serve as an optimization for READ COMMITTED isolation level and will get rid of the basic implementation)

- #5680 (detailed roadmap present in the github issue)

This has been asked in different ways:
Issues from @RunningJon - #9465, #9469
Issues from @bllewell - #1985

### Phase 4 - Possible future enhancements

- #9517 (Required for SKIP LOCKED in SERIALIZABLE isolation level. Also allows for higher concurrency than coarse table/tablet locks)
- #9518

issue.title: [DocDB] Follower Reads not working as expected on 2.12.x.x with Read Committed.

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-2654](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-2654)
### Description

When called inside a Read only transaction block we seem to be updating the timestamp for follower reads only on the first statement (after begin transaction). 

Subsequent statements seem to adjust the read point to "current time". But then don't update it to account for follower reads/staleness.

This can cause bad perf if follower reads are enabled while using Read Committed (requires the gflag to be enabled).

body: We just ran into this. I assume it'll be ported back to 2.12? I also know that 2.14 is coming up so we're also considering just turning off read committed for now until 2.14.
